subject: REQUIRED: Circuit-breaker & temporary routing for Medisys streaming timeouts

From: monica_patel@redwood.com

Date: 2026-12-15T09:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RE: intermittent streaming timeouts (production)

Triage notes (live):

- Root observation: high client-driven retry rate creating hot tails on the streaming dispatcher. Idle streams are being torn down by the edge ~20s after the client stops ACKing, which causes clients to re-open with aggressive backoff disabled in several SDK versions. That pattern is producing a retry storm (many short-lived open-streams) and exhausting connection slots on a subset of inference pods.
- 5xx pattern is primarily 503/524 during the surge window; internal logs show queueing and occasional OOM for quantized workloads.
- Correlation: ~12% of Medisys sessions originated from older SDK (v1.4.2) that doesn't honor server SIG_KEEPALIVE; clients assume connection failure faster than we do.

Immediate mitigation proposed (can be enacted in parallel):
1) Route Medisys production traffic to warmed Dedicated pool (same model spec) for 1 hour to relieve pressure.
2) Enable temporary circuit-breaker at API-gateway: if a client sees >6 failures in 60s, return deterministic 429 with retry-after and suppress automatic server-side retries to prevent amplification.
3) Push a short client-side patch request to Medisys to enable exponential backoff and keepalive.

I'll stand by to implement 1 & 2 pending Rafael approval and Evelyn to coordinate infra.

— Monica

Attachments referenced: grafana-5xx-dashboard.png

Subject: Post-incident: remediation plan & executive notes (Medisys)

Tom / Ellie — status update and next steps after the Dec 15 incident. Summary: short-lived retry storm from older SDK + idle disconnects caused elevated 429/5xx rates during a PST morning window. Root causes and actions below.

Root cause:
- Client SDK v1.4.2 does not honor server keepalive semantics; clients aggressively re-open streams after ~20s.
- This produced a retry amplification loop that pushed a subset of inference pods over queue limits, producing 503/524s.

What we did (immediate):
- Routed Medisys traffic to warmed Dedicated pool for 3 hours to drain queued work and restore tail latency.
- Deployed an API-gateway circuit-breaker rule to return deterministic 429+Retry-After for clients exceeding failure thresholds to prevent server-side retries.
- Increased autoscale aggressiveness for the impacted pool for the recovery window.

Planned remediation (next 30 days):
- Client: Medisys to ship SDK patch (v1.5.0) that enables exponential backoff and explicit socket keepalive (we shared a patch PR). Target: 2027-01-05.
- Server: Implement per-connection heartbeat and reduced idle disconnect threshold configurable per-customer (default 45s) so older clients have a larger grace window. Target: 2027-01-12.
- Ops: Add a real-time per-customer retry amplification detector and automated routing policy. Target: 2027-01-08.

Compensation: we agreed to review credits. I’ve flagged this to Revenue Ops; Rafael will follow up with formal credit proposal and HubSpot deal update.

Attached: grafana-5xx-dashboard.png, stream-logs-2026-12-15.tar.gz (anonymized).

If helpful, I can prepare a short executive one-pager for your leadership summarizing risk and proposed SLAs.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
